content: VFM_01_Foundations: what an arrow carries — components, basis, a frame to read it in
Vectors_Act1_WhatAVectorIs: the same, at the scale of a room you walk
VFM_02_Operations: two arrows meet — add, subtract, dot, cross, project, torque
Vectors_Act2_VectorArithmetic: arithmetic you cross on foot, with the XL lasers
VFM_04_Fields: an arrow at every point — flow, weather, magnets, vortices
Vectors_Act3_FieldsAndMotion: standing in the field while it moves you
VFM_03_Motion: the arrow over time — velocity, acceleration, trajectory
VFM_05_Launch: aiming it — catapult, turret, mortar, the arc you predict
Vectors_Act4a_KineticForces: the walk that pushes back — centrifuge, drag, orbit
VFM_06_Springs: the force that returns what it is given
VFM_07_Gravity: attraction, two bodies, three, and the chaos after
VFM_08_Arena: force against force — collision, reflection, targets
Vectors_Act4b_Oscillation: the pendulum hall and the spring tower, at building scale
Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace: a force you stand inside — the loop closes on rung 1
forces.demonstration: See vectors as arrows in space. Add them head-to-tail. Feel dot product measure alignment. Watch cross product create perpendicular vectors. Then feel gravity pull you down. Push objects and feel resistance. Watch attraction and repulsion create orbits and explosions.
forces.description: The fundamental language of 3D space meets the physics that brings it to life. Vectors encode direction and magnitudeâ€”the building blocks of everything spatial. Forces convert those vectors into motion through Newton's laws. Master vectors, master forces, master the physical world.

learning_objectives: Coordinate systems and spatial reasoning in 3D
Vector components: x, y, z as decomposed direction
Magnitude: length as âˆš(xÂ² + yÂ² + zÂ²)
Addition and subtraction: combining and differencing vectors
Cross product: creating perpendicular vectors, torque, normals
Projection and reflection: mirrors and collisions
Vector fields: spatial functions mapping position to direction
F = ma: Force equals mass times acceleration
Friction and drag: resistance to motion
Attraction and repulsion: inverse square laws
Particle systems: many bodies under forces
N-body dynamics: gravitational chaos from simple rules

Derivative as instantaneous rate of change: velocity is the rate of position; acceleration is the rate of velocity. F = ma is calculus made physical — the calculus substrate named at change (seq 4.5) carried into the world here.
forces.name: Vectors & Forces: From Direction to Dynamics
forces.qfep_connection: Vectors define system statesâ€”the S in QFEP. Forces introduce changeâ€”they drive the temporal evolution Ï†Î”E(S,t). Together, vectors and forces are the complete grammar of physical motion: direction encodes where, magnitude encodes how much, and F=ma encodes why things change.
forces.truth: Direction + magnitude = vector. F = ma. Acceleration is the only thing you feel. Position and velocity are states; force is what changes them.

artifact_groups.rationale: Three islands of vector fundamentals: components, magnitude, addition and subtraction. Entry point for the combined vectors+forces sequence.
Three islands of advanced vector operations: dot product, cross product, projection/reflection. Builds on foundation components.
Targeting turrets, weather fields, and force vectors across three islands. Applied vector usage in game-like contexts.
Four islands of advanced applications: torque, dynamic simulations, steering, projectile throwing.
Force superposition, work-energy theorem, and momentum conservation in one diamond arena. Bridges vectors to forces.
Three islands of fundamental forces: Newton's laws, projectile motion, friction. Jump pads as embodied projectile physics.
Four islands of force systems: attractors, force fields, springs, particles. Clockwise circuit via jump pads. Callbacks to vector basics.
N-body dynamics and strange attractors: deterministic chaos from simple rules. Two islands of complexity.
Grand finale: drone combat, physics destruction sandbox, and exhibition gallery. Applied forces across three massive arenas with callbacks to throwing and vectors.

forces.deferred_reason: THE FOLD, 2026-08-25 (Palle: 'too many maps but we do not want to lose any essential artifacts'). forces listed 30 maps because it held THREE rival ladders and a junk drawer. Retired here: the older Vector*/Forces* ladder (9 rooms, superseded by the museum) and 7 bench/test rooms that were never curriculum (Console_Test, Reformed_Instruments, Force_Props_Sandbox, Force_Preview, Sky_Climb, Void_Crossing, Chamber_Forces). Every token they held was judged one by one in doc/folds/forces.json and the verdict is checkable: python tools/fold_ledger.py --sequence=forces --plan=doc/folds/forces.json --check

taxonomy._readme: THE LADDER (2026-08-25), five rungs at TWO SCALES. The Acts and the VFM museum were not rivals — measured, they share only 22 of 169 tokens — so both survive: the museum is the BENCH (an operation at arm's length) and the Acts are the BUILDING (the same operation at the scale of a room you walk through). Folding them into one room each would have flattened the sequence's own claim, the way folding color's hand/set/space would have flattened colour's. Closes as a LOOP: rung 5 is a force you STAND INSIDE, which is rung 1's arrow with the walker put inside it.
taxonomy.0_recalled_unit: the vector itself is NOT taught here. primitives is sequence 1 — 'points, lines, planes, and basic vectors' — so an arrow with a length and a direction arrives already known. Like color's unit, it is a threshold the walk crosses, not a room it stops in.
taxonomy.1_quantity: what does an arrow carry? — magnitude and direction, a basis, a coordinate frame. BENCH VFM_01_Foundations · BUILDING Vectors_Act1_WhatAVectorIs (length_lantern, CoordinateSystem3M, vector_normalize_demo).
taxonomy.2_operation: what do two of them do to each other? — add, subtract, dot, cross, project, torque. BENCH VFM_02_Operations · BUILDING Vectors_Act2_VectorArithmetic. The XL exhibits here DELEGATE to the algorithm scenes (vector_dot_product_xl -> VectorDotProduct at 5x), which is why the fold had to follow delegate edges before it could count anything.
taxonomy.3_field: what if there is one at every point? — flow, weather, magnets, vortices. BENCH VFM_04_Fields · BUILDING Vectors_Act3_FieldsAndMotion.
taxonomy.4_motion: what does an arrow do over time? — velocity, acceleration, trajectory, launch. BENCH VFM_03_Motion + VFM_05_Launch · BUILDING Vectors_Act4a_KineticForces. This is where CHANGE comes back: velocity is the first derivative and acceleration the second, so the rung is the calculus sequence read in a body.
taxonomy.5_force: what changes the motion? — F = ma: springs, gravity, collision, oscillation, and finally a force as a PLACE. BENCH VFM_06_Springs + VFM_07_Gravity + VFM_08_Arena · BUILDING Vectors_Act4b_Oscillation + Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace. Closes the loop — force is the second derivative of position, so the last rung hands the walk back to change.
